# package dnp3

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3"
```

Package dnp3 is the module root of a pure Go implementation of DNP3 (IEEE 1815-2012), the SCADA protocol between masters and outstations in electric, water and oil and gas utilities.

Applications import the subpackages:

  - [github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/client): the master: integrity and event polls, unsolicited responses, controls with select-before- operate, time synchronization, restarts, file transfer, secure authentication, automatic reconnect and retries
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/server](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/server): the outstation: a point database with event buffers per class, request handling, unsolicited responses, controls and command events, file transfer, secure authentication with statistics, and the dual end point
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/secauth](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/secauth): Secure Authentication version 5: users and keys, MACs, the AES key wrap, statistics
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/app](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/app): the application layer codec and the object library
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/transport): the transport function
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/link](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/link): the data link layer codec

This package holds what client and server share: the sentinel and typed errors, the [Logger](#type-logger) and [Metrics](#type-metrics) interfaces and the channel [State](#type-state).

Docs: README.md, API.md (public API), ARCHITECTURE.md, ERRORS.md (error semantics), OBSERVABILITY.md (logging and metrics), INTEROPERABILITY.md (conformance and interop coverage), SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, RELEASE.md (changelog).

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrClosed reports an operation on a client, server or association
	// that was closed by the application.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("dnp3: closed")

	// ErrNotConnected reports a request on a client that has no
	// established channel.
	ErrNotConnected = errors.New("dnp3: not connected")

	// ErrConnectFailed reports that a client could not establish its
	// channel: the dial, the TLS handshake or the opening of the serial
	// port failed. The underlying error is wrapped alongside it.
	ErrConnectFailed = errors.New("dnp3: connect failed")

	// ErrConnectionLost reports that the peer closed the channel or the
	// transport failed while a request was in progress.
	ErrConnectionLost = errors.New("dnp3: connection lost")

	// ErrTimeout reports that the peer did not answer within the response
	// timeout (client) or did not confirm within the confirm timeout
	// (server), or that a link layer confirmation did not arrive.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("dnp3: timeout")

	// ErrProtocol reports a peer that violated the protocol: a response
	// whose objects do not match the request (a control echo that differs,
	// a missing or unexpected object, a wrong file block), or a link layer
	// answer that does not fit. Awaiting a response, a fragment with an
	// unexpected sequence number is ignored; during a multi-fragment
	// response, an unexpected fragment abandons the response with
	// ErrProtocol.
	ErrProtocol = errors.New("dnp3: protocol violation")

	// ErrBusy reports a request that cannot be issued because the
	// association has reached its queue limit.
	ErrBusy = errors.New("dnp3: too many pending requests")

	// ErrInvalidOption reports an option value a client or server cannot
	// be constructed with.
	ErrInvalidOption = errors.New("dnp3: invalid option")

	// ErrAuthentication reports a failure of secure authentication: a MAC
	// that does not verify, a key that is not initialized, or a challenge
	// that was not answered. An *[AuthError] carries the code the peer sent.
	ErrAuthentication = errors.New("dnp3: authentication failed")
)
```

Sentinel errors shared by the client and the server. They are usually wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

### type ContextLogger

```go
type ContextLogger interface {
	Logger

	DebugContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

ContextLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with context-aware structured logging, so that a handler can pick trace and span identifiers out of the context. When the Logger also implements ContextLogger, entries that belong to a request are logged with the context the request was called with.

### type FieldLogger

```go
type FieldLogger interface {
	Logger

	// With returns a logger that adds the given fields to every entry.
	With(keysAndValues ...any) FieldLogger

	DebugKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

FieldLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with structured key-value logging. When the Logger given to a client or server also implements FieldLogger, the library logs through it: every entry is a constant message plus fields such as "component", "remote", "outstation", "master" and "error", instead of one formatted string. [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) returns such a logger.

keysAndValues alternate string keys and values, as in log/slog.

#### func NewSlogFieldLogger

```go
func NewSlogFieldLogger(h slog.Handler) FieldLogger
```

NewSlogFieldLogger is [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) with the result typed as a [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger), for callers that want to add fields with With before handing the logger to a client or server. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

### type Logger

```go
type Logger interface {
	Debugf(format string, args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warnf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
}
```

Logger is the logging interface accepted by the client and the server. Implement it to integrate any logging library.

Logging is silent by default. Methods are invoked synchronously on the protocol path and must not block.

#### func NewSlogLogger

```go
func NewSlogLogger(h slog.Handler) Logger
```

NewSlogLogger wraps a slog.Handler. The result implements [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger) and [ContextLogger](#type-contextlogger), so the library logs structured fields through it; messages are only built when the handler is enabled for their level. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

#### func NewStdLogger

```go
func NewStdLogger(l *log.Logger) Logger
```

NewStdLogger wraps a standard library logger. Each message is prefixed with its level. A nil l logs to os.Stderr with the standard flags.


NopLogger returns a Logger that discards everything.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnConnect is called when a transport connection is established or
	// a serial port opened.
	OnConnect(remote net.Addr)

	// OnDisconnect is called when a channel ends. err is nil when the
	// application closed it.
	OnDisconnect(remote net.Addr, err error)

	// OnFrameSent is called after a link frame was written. size is its
	// length on the wire in octets.
	OnFrameSent(remote net.Addr, f *link.Frame, size int)

	// OnFrameReceived is called for every link frame read from the peer.
	OnFrameReceived(remote net.Addr, f *link.Frame, size int)

	// OnFramingError is called when octets were skipped or a frame was
	// discarded: a bad start sequence, a CRC error, an invalid length.
	OnFramingError(remote net.Addr, err error)

	// OnFragmentSent is called after an application fragment was handed
	// to the transport function. size is its length in octets.
	OnFragmentSent(remote net.Addr, f *app.Fragment, size int)

	// OnFragmentReceived is called for every fragment that was
	// reassembled and decoded.
	OnFragmentReceived(remote net.Addr, f *app.Fragment, size int)

	// OnDecodeError is called when a reassembled fragment, or a segment,
	// could not be decoded and was dropped.
	OnDecodeError(remote net.Addr, err error)
}
```

Metrics is an optional callback interface for observing the channels and the traffic of a client or a server. A nil Metrics disables collection.

The methods are called synchronously on the protocol path, possibly from several goroutines at once; implementations must be safe for concurrent use and must not block (increment a counter, send on a buffered channel). Frames and fragments passed to them must not be retained or modified.

Embed [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics) to implement only the callbacks you need and to stay compatible when methods are added.

### type RequestMetrics

```go
type RequestMetrics interface {
	// OnRequest is called before a request is sent.
	OnRequest(remote net.Addr, outstation uint16, fc app.FunctionCode)

	// OnRequestDone is called with the final outcome. err is nil on
	// success; classify failures with errors.Is and errors.As
	// (*IINError, *CommandError, ErrTimeout, ...).
	OnRequestDone(remote net.Addr, outstation uint16, fc app.FunctionCode, duration time.Duration, err error)

	// OnRetry is called when attempt (1 for the first) failed with err and
	// the request is about to be tried again.
	OnRetry(remote net.Addr, outstation uint16, fc app.FunctionCode, attempt int, err error)
}
```

RequestMetrics is an optional extension of [Metrics](#type-metrics) for a client. When the value given to client.WithMetrics also implements it, the client reports every request: polls, commands, time synchronization, file operations.

OnRequest fires once before the first attempt and OnRequestDone once with the final outcome, whose duration includes retries and their delays. OnRetry fires for each attempt that failed and will be repeated.

remote is the address of the channel, or nil while the client has never been connected. outstation is the link address of the outstation.

### type ServerMetrics

```go
type ServerMetrics interface {
	// OnHandled is called after a request was handled, with the time
	// from its reception to the end of the handler calls.
	OnHandled(remote net.Addr, fc app.FunctionCode, duration time.Duration)

	// OnEventsDiscarded is called when an event buffer overflowed and n
	// events of the class (1..3) were discarded.
	OnEventsDiscarded(class int, n int)

	// OnUnsolicited is called after an unsolicited response was confirmed
	// (err == nil) or abandoned.
	OnUnsolicited(remote net.Addr, events int, err error)
}
```

ServerMetrics is an optional extension of [Metrics](#type-metrics) for a server. When the value given to server.WithMetrics also implements it, the server reports every request it handled and every event it had to discard.
